scope: Fix native ANGLE/D3D11 X4000 in the analytic fog shared by asteroids. Diagnose the separate belt-volume cost; no raymarch performance or quality change shipped.
implementation: ringDustPieceMask keeps its original formulas and two return expressions inside explicit if/else branches. The existing CPU mirror is unchanged. Browser diagnostics reject X4000 for this function.

method.gpu: AMD Radeon Graphics / ANGLE D3D11, native Chrome 155, 1280x720 DPR 1
method.assets: Real scenario resources from Yandex S3, dev build
method.frozenInputs: Stop engine; clone real dust uniforms/camera/world transform; preserve uploaded profile textures; copy scene depth into a private Float render target.
method.rendering: Actual dust proxy and fragment source, unsmoothed Float RGBA output with NoBlending, six warmups and 32 native elapsed GPU queries per variant, baseline repeated at end.
method.comparison: L1 error of raw HDR RGBA relative to baseline sum of absolute components, plus maximum component error. This is not final composited image error.
method.caveats: Each scenario view is frozen independently per run. GPU timings are isolated dust draw costs, not total frame times or production performance. Disabled effects are diagnostic ablations, not fixes.

conclusions.rejectedCandidates: Skipping zero-density samples was slightly slower. Explicit texture LOD and a static 16-iteration upper bound produced effectively unchanged timings. All three had exact raw HDR equality in the tested frozen views.
conclusions.remaining: The clump noise dominates volume cost. Quality-preserving caching or depth-aware reconstruction still needs a separate experiment. Audit item 16 remains open.
